description: Van’dan 4 lise öğrencisi ve bir öğretmenden oluşan ekibimiz, robotik ve uzay keşfi tutkusuyla bir araya geldi. Robotik projelerinde edindiğimiz deneyimi NASA’nın açık verileriyle buluşturarak gerçek dünya ve uzay problemlerine yaratıcı çözümler üretmeyi hedefliyoruz. Hata yapmaktan çekinmeyen, her zorluğu öğrenme fırsatı olarak gören bir ekibiz. Bizim için bu yarışma sadece bir proje değil; yıldızlara uzanan yolculuğun ilk adımı.
summary:
ASTRA-MED AI is an AI-powered, offline health monitoring and decision-support system designed to protect astronauts during long-duration space missions, where communication delays or interruptions can limit access to medical assistance from Earth.

We developed a prototype that integrates real-time physiological monitoring, intelligent risk detection, and a four-agent artificial intelligence architecture designed to operate locally on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano. Three specialized AI agents independently evaluate astronauts' health conditions using sensor data, including heart rate, body temperature, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate. A fourth agent acts as a medical council coordinator, combining their assessments to generate risk alerts and actionable recommendations.

Our system is designed to monitor multiple astronauts simultaneously, simulate potential medical emergencies, and generate health reports for mission control, even when communication is temporarily unavailable.

By addressing NASA's challenge of creating health monitoring software for astronauts, ASTRA-MED AI aims to reduce dependence on Earth-based medical support, improve early risk detection, and enhance crew safety.

Our vision is simple: Even when communication with Earth is lost, no astronaut should face a medical emergency alone.
details:
ASTRA-MED AI: Autonomous Health Monitoring and AI-Powered Medical Decision Support for Astronauts

Project Overview

ASTRA-MED AI is an offline, AI-powered health monitoring and medical decision-support system developed by Team URARTU SPACE for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Our project addresses the challenge of creating health monitoring software for astronauts during long-duration space missions, where communication delays, limited medical resources, and unexpected health emergencies can threaten crew safety.

Our goal is to provide astronauts with an intelligent health monitoring assistant that can assess physiological conditions, detect potential risks, and offer immediate decision support without depending on continuous communication with Earth.

How Does It Work?

ASTRA-MED AI combines physiological sensor monitoring, embedded computing, and a four-agent artificial intelligence architecture.

The system is designed to process astronauts' vital signs, including heart rate, body temperature, blood oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate. These measurements are analyzed to identify abnormal patterns and potential health risks.

At the center of our architecture is the NVIDIA Jetson Nano, an embedded AI computing platform selected to support local processing without relying on cloud infrastructure.

Our four-agent architecture consists of:

  1. Three Specialized Medical AI Agents: Evaluate physiological measurements, investigate potential health abnormalities, and generate independent risk assessments.
  2. One Medical Council Coordinator: Reviews the assessments from the three specialized agents, evaluates potential inconsistencies, and combines their findings into a unified decision-support recommendation.

The system also includes a medical assistant interface, allowing astronauts to receive health-related guidance. Its mission control dashboard is designed to monitor multiple crew members, visualize physiological changes, display risk alerts, and generate health reports.

Our current prototype demonstrates these functions through simulated astronaut health scenarios. Full onboard deployment and clinical validation remain future development stages.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRA-MED AI aims to improve astronaut safety by enabling earlier recognition of physiological abnormalities and providing locally available health decision support.

One of its primary advantages is independence from continuous Earth communication. During missions to the Moon, Mars, or other distant destinations, communication delays and interruptions may prevent immediate consultation with ground-based medical specialists.

By processing health information locally, our proposed system could help astronauts identify emerging risks and make more informed decisions while awaiting professional medical guidance.

The architecture is also designed to support multiple astronauts simultaneously, making it relevant to future crewed space missions.

Beyond space exploration, the same approach could potentially be adapted for isolated research stations, submarines, remote healthcare facilities, and other environments with limited connectivity.

Tools, Technologies, and Hardware

Our project integrates several technological components:

  • NVIDIA Jetson Nano: Target embedded computing platform for offline AI processing.
  • Artificial Intelligence and Multi-Agent Architecture: Four coordinated agents designed for specialized health evaluation and consolidated decision support.
  • Physiological Sensor Integration: A monitoring architecture incorporating heart rate, temperature, oxygen saturation, and respiratory measurements.
  • Health Monitoring Dashboard: An interactive interface displaying astronaut health indicators, simulated ECG signals, warnings, and AI-generated assessments.
  • Health Scenario Simulation: Simulated physiological conditions used to demonstrate system behavior under different health-risk scenarios.
  • NASA Human Research Program Resources: Reference material describing the five hazards of human spaceflight, used to identify relevant astronaut health challenges.

Our prototype focuses on the integration of these components into a unified health monitoring workflow. The specific programming languages, software frameworks, and deployed AI models should be identified from the implementation repository rather than assumed.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

The distinguishing feature of ASTRA-MED AI is its proposed combination of offline embedded artificial intelligence, collaborative medical agents, and multi-astronaut health monitoring.

Instead of relying on a single AI assessment, our architecture introduces a medical council approach in which three specialized agents contribute evaluations and a fourth agent coordinates their findings.

This structure is intended to make health assessments more organized and interpretable. Its actual performance advantages will need to be established through comparative testing.

Another creative aspect is the emphasis on performing AI processing directly aboard the spacecraft. Rather than sending every physiological measurement to Earth for analysis, the proposed architecture brings decision-support capabilities closer to the astronaut.

Our prototype also allows us to simulate medical scenarios, observe how the monitoring interface responds, and explore how AI agents could contribute to crew health management.

Design Considerations and Challenges

During development, our team considered several constraints associated with space missions:

Communication limitations: The system should maintain essential monitoring and analysis functions when communication with Earth is unavailable.

Limited computing resources: AI models must be optimized for the memory, processing capacity, and power constraints of embedded hardware.

Medical reliability: Incorrect recommendations could have serious consequences. Therefore, clinical validation, uncertainty handling, and appropriate human oversight are essential before real-world medical deployment.

Multiple crew members: The architecture should support individual astronaut profiles while enabling mission-wide health monitoring.
